mediastinitis by ~4–6 h, severe by ~8 h, then sepsis and instability with very high mortality → early operative management, ideally within ~12 h.

no single treatment — ABC + treat the cause; observe if stable and non-progressive. Urgent intervention if vital signs deteriorate or emphysema expands rapidly: chest tube ± suction (check any existing drain is patent); an extra tube for a large leak; bronchoscopy for massive unexplained emphysema after intubation; uncontrolled leak despite two chest tubes → thoracotomy.

the flail segment moves in the opposite direction to the rest of the chest wall — can significantly impair breathing and injure the underlying lung.
